CausalChain: High inflammatory cytokine levels in the tumor microenvironment -> Induction of altered glycosylation and phosphorylation of CLDN18.2 -> Enhanced disruption of tight junctions and increased epitope exposure -> Modified binding characteristics of CLDN18.2 -> Improved immune effector engagement by CLDN18.2-targeted therapies
Hypothesis: Inflammation-induced post-translational modifications of CLDN18.2 in tumor cells enhance its surface exposure and alter therapeutic targetability; thus, pharmacological modulation of these modifications will synergize with CLDN18.2-directed immunotherapies to improve treatment outcomes in solid tumors.
Abstract: Recent studies have demonstrated that Claudin18.2 (CLDN18.2) is aberrantly expressed on the surface of several solid tumors due to disruptions in normal tight junction integrity. Its selective expression in malignant tissues has prompted its targeting via various immunotherapeutic strategies, including monoclonal antibodies, CAR‐T cells, and antibody–drug conjugates. However, there remains an underexplored area regarding the regulation of CLDN18.2 through post‐translational modifications within the tumor microenvironment. Here, we propose that the inflammatory milieu characteristic of many solid tumors alters the glycosylation and phosphorylation states of CLDN18.2, thereby enhancing its cell surface exposure and modifying its binding affinity to therapeutic agents. Strategically modulating these modifications may potentiate the efficacy of existing CLDN18.2‐targeted therapies by improving immune cell engagement and antibody binding.
